chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira entered upon him and said to him, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, I have a daughter who is capable/standing for me in all matters, and she is a first-born. Can I make my Hajj for her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, its reward will be for her, and there will be for you the like of that, and nothing will be diminished from her reward.'

key_terms.قَيِّمَةٌ: Capable/standing for me (acting as my representative)

ai.seo_question: Can I perform Hajj for my living daughter and will she receive the full reward?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the permissibility of a living relative performing Hajj on behalf of another, a practice distinct from the Hajj of necessity (Hajj al-Niyabah) for those who cannot perform it themselves. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the designated daughter retains her full spiritual reward while the father simultaneously accrues an equal share, demonstrating the cumulative nature of good deeds in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the communal and familial dimensions of worship, where one's piety can extend benefits to capable kin.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Safwan Al Jammal who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so Al-Haris Bin Al-Mugheira came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May my father be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, and my mother! For me is a daughter who stands for me upon everything, and she is a first-born. Can I make my Hajj to be for her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its Recompense would happen to be for her, and there would happen to be for you the like of that, and there would not be a reduction from its Recompense, of anything’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following: “I once went to visit abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah also came and said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause. I have a daughter who looks after every one of my things and she is the first one. Can I assign my al-Hajj for her?
He (the Imam) said, ‘The reward for al-Hajj will be for her and you will have a similar reward without any reduction in her reward.’”
